podcast.title: Avatar of Roots-Oriented Rock
podcast.body: Edmonds quickly became recognized as the "avatar" of the roots-oriented approach to rock music. He was a central figure at the "crux" of the pub rock scene and went on to produce albums for several bands within this scene, including Ducks Deluxe and the American band Eggs Over Easy. "Dave Edmonds soon became the avatar of this Rootsie approach."

srcs.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia

podcast.title: Formation of Rockpile
podcast.body: He formed an on-again, off-again band called Rockpile with Nick Lowe, named after Edmonds' 1972 LP. While the band played gigs more frequently than they recorded, they were instrumental in infusing retro rock elements into what would eventually become the New Wave sound. "Lo and Edmonds formed an on-again off-again band called Rockpile, named for Edmonds 1972 LP."

srcs.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia

podcast.title: Shift to New Wave
podcast.body: Around 1978, Dave Edmonds himself transitioned his musical direction towards New Wave. "Dave Edmunds, too, had shifted in a new wavy direction."

srcs.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia
